content_html_sanitized:
Posted April 26, 2004
Blunt Bros, the popular Vancouver smoke-easy, was completely destroyed by a fire of suspicious origin Sunday morning. The upstairs office of the seed company owned by the same people was also lost. They had been operating without police interference since a raid in January of 1991.
See
Blunt Bros. Update: They Reopen After Narks Steal Over C$10,000 in Pipes and Other Merchandise Without Leaving A Receipt.

There is nothing left of the 1898 building except a pile of rubble, level with the street. For a while it looked as if the whole block might be lost, but the Vancouver Fire Department put massive resources into fighting the blaze.

Those first on the scene said that the fire appeared to have started in dumpsters in the alley. (Vancouver has a serious arson problem, but grow-op fires make the headlines. The fire department also reported that someone had a small grow-op in the building, but this is Vancouver!)

The BC Marijuana Party Book Store and Pot-TV Studio next door suffered some smoke and water damage, but will reopen as soon as the electric power is restored. (Marc Emery's seed business was unaffected by the fire.)

Ironically, the New Amsterdam, also owned by the Blunt Bros. group, had just been closed a few weeks ago because it was not doing enough business. It suffered minimal damage, and is now expected to reopen soon, presumably by the same group. The crowds pick-up substantially in the summer, as does Vancouver tourism generally.

Last year it was rumored that Henk DeVries, the owner of the Bulldog chain in Amsterdam, was interested in picking up the lease, but he apparently decided that the block would not support two such places. That tells us something about the Vancouver scene.

The New Amsterdam was always aimed at an older/quieter crowd, but that was not enough to make a profit. Neither Blunt Bros. nor the New Amsterdam sold weed, but both tolerated cannabis smoking. For visiting Americans such an island of tolerance was a cultural adventure, not quite on the level of Holland's coffee shops, but astonishing to those raised in the land of the (drug) Free, and Home Of The Extremely Paranoid.

Actually, there are places nearby that do sell weed, one popular youth hangout is even reported to have a house-dealer in the summer. There is also a new cannabis-friendly café (smoking but no selling) on Granville Street in the theatre district, but Blunt's and the Amsterdam provided a great place to meet visiting friends. In that regard, they played a vital role in the Vancouver cannabis world, so it is important that the New Amsterdam reopens.

Vancouver has become so cannabis tolerant that the pot-block is nothing too special for the natives. There are small restaurants that tolerate cannabis in their outdoor smoking areas later in the evening, and one sees people casually passing joints as they walk or sit along the popular seawall. The evolution of freedom in Vancouver will someday be the subject of serious study, but right now it remains serious work.
From 1999 see
The Evolution of Freedom In " Vansterdam " -- Special To Marijuananews
(MarijuanaNews note: The " Amsterdam Coffee House Hemporium " mentioned in that story is not the same as the New Amsterdam.)
